subject: Renewal: proposal to convert burst credits into reserved commit + ramp / price-protection ask
messages:
From: Jon Hargreaves <jonh@atlashealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Renewal baseline + converting burst credits to reserved commit

Hi Laura —

We’re getting around to planning our budget for next year and wanted to loop you in early on renewal. We’ve been running in a mixed model (hosted + burst credits) and would like to explore converting a chunk of our remaining burst credits into a 12-month reserved commit so we can justify the spend to finance. Key asks from our side:

- Can you convert N of our remaining burst credits into a reserved GPU pool commitment?
- What price protection can Redwood offer if we sign now but ramp slowly (we anticipate 2–3 months to reach steady throughput)?
- What discount bands are available for a 12-month commit vs a 24-month?
- Can you guarantee throughput tiers (p95 latency and tokens/sec) for the committed pool or do we need an uplift add-on?

Also copying our procurement lead, Maya.

Thanks —
Jon
Head of ML Infrastructure, AtlasHealth
jonh@atlashealth.com
(555) 213-7801

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Renewal baseline + converting burst credits to reserved commit

Jon —

Thanks for the heads up. Good news: we can structure a conversion path that preserves much of the remaining burst value while giving you the predictability of a reserved pool. High-level options below; I attached an initial proposal (ATLAS_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf) and a proposed pool layout (SOW_GPU-Pool-Layout.xlsx).

Option A — Immediate 12‑month commit (recommended)
- Convert up to 65% of remaining burst value into an equivalent GPU-hour commit.
- Pricing: effective unit price = current burst rate * 0.88 (12% discount).
- Ramp: 90 days to full throughput, with staged ramp targets (week 4/8/12).
- SLA: standard Dedicated SLA; additional throughput SLO add-on available.

Option B — 12‑month commit with price-protection window (what Maya asked about)
- Same conversion mechanics as A, but price locked for 9 months; if wholesale prices fall after 9 months we offer a one-time reconciliation credit.
- Slightly lower discount (10%).

Option C — 24‑month commit (best unit economics)
- 16% discount on effective unit price; 6‑month ramp.

Technical notes (Ben / Priyom can expand): throughput guarantees depend on pool sizing (GPU type + concurrency). We should align on target tokens/sec per model and tail latency SLOs to size the pool correctly.

Next steps: If you like Option A/ B/ C, flag which one and we’ll (1) prepare a formal Order Form + SOW, (2) seed a ramp schedule, and (3) generate a DocuSign link for signatures.

Best,
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: Renewal baseline + converting burst credits to reserved commit (sizing notes)

Folks —

Quick sizing and SLO notes for the proposal:
- Baseline model: medbert-v2 and a TTS pipe. Based on Atlas recent telemetry, peak concurrent streams ~60, 95th latency target 300ms on 1024 tokens.
- Recommendation: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline committed pool to meet p95 at expected concurrency with room for 10% headroom.
- If you choose the 12% discount band (Option A), we can include an automatically-triggered 2-week burst buffer for the first month to absorb ramp spikes.
- Throughput SLO: we can commit to a throughput tier (tokens/sec) with an availability SLA; explicit credits for missed monthly throughput targets can be added to the order form.

I added a suggested ramp schedule in the SOW (see SOW_GPU-Pool-Layout.xlsx). Happy to jump on a 30m technical call with Jon + Maya to finalize numbers.

—Ben

ben_carter@redwood.ai

Laura —

Thanks for the options. Procurement questions / redlines from our side before we can route to legal & finance: 

1) Price protection: we need a 9-month firm price protection window once we sign (we can accept reconciliation credit afterwards). Please confirm in writing.
2) Ramp credit: during the first 90 days we expect a staged ramp. If Redwood misses the staged throughput targets, we require service credits applied to the next invoice (standard % schedule).
3) Conversion math: please include a line-by-line export showing how remaining burst credits were converted into committed GPU-hours (so we can justify to audit).
4) Change management: we want the option to expand the pool mid-term at the same effective unit price band if we sign within 30 days.

Also: can you provide a DocuSign order form and an itemized order that our finance team can plug into the PO?

Thanks —
Maya Singh

Maya / Jon —

Appreciate the clarity — we can accommodate all four asks. Summary of commitments (we will reflect these in the Order Form + SOW):

1) Price protection: we’ll lock pricing for 9 months from signature. If market unit pricing for the selected GPU tier falls during the protection period, we’ll provide a one-time reconciliation credit equal to the net difference (not to exceed 5% of the committed value).

2) Ramp credit schedule: we’ll include a staged throughput SLO with monthly targets for months 1–3; missed targets will generate invoice credits per the following schedule: month1 5%, month2 3%, month3 2% applied to the following invoice. 

3) Conversion math: attached is the line-by-line conversion appendix in the Proposal (see ATLAS_Renewal_Proposal_v3.pdf). It details burst token/hour -> GPU-hour math.

4) Expansion option: if Atlas signs within 30 days, additional capacity added mid-term can be added at the same effective unit price band (subject to minimum increment of 2 GPUs).

Concessions: we can offer an 8% effective discount on Option A (12‑month commit) if Atlas signs and returns DocuSign within 7 business days. Otherwise standard 12% band applies. 

I uploaded a pre-filled DocuSign order form and a marked-up order form for your legal to review (DocuSign-ATLAS-OrderForm-link.txt). If you want, we can schedule 30 minutes with legal to run the redlines this week.

Best,
Laura Bennett
